name: What should be included in a pool contractor proposal?

mainEntity.name: What should a pool contractor proposal include so there are no surprise costs?
mainEntity.text: What should a pool contractor proposal include so there are no surprise costs?

acceptedAnswer.text: A detailed pool contractor proposal should clearly define the work from demolition through startup. It should include pool dimensions, shell construction, tile and coping, decking, drainage, plumbing, electrical, equipment brands and model numbers, lighting, automation, and any spa or water feature details. The proposal should also state who handles permits, inspections, cleanup, haul-away, and startup chemistry. Just as important, it should list exclusions and allowances so the homeowner knows what is not included. Hidden costs usually appear when a proposal is generic about utility upgrades, finish selections, access conditions, grading, or retaining walls. The payment schedule and change-order policy should also be written clearly. If two proposals differ dramatically, the one with the most detail is usually easier to trust because it exposes where the real scope and risk sit.
acceptedAnswer.description: A strong proposal should list the full scope, materials, equipment brands and model numbers, permit responsibilities, payment schedule, change-order process, warranty terms, cleanup, and exclusions. If a proposal is vague on finishes, utilities, or site work, it is not complete enough for comparison.
